exercises.text: A drop of oil with a volume of $1$ mm$^3$ is placed on the surface of water. The area over which it spreads cannot exceed $3$ m$^2$. Use these data to estimate the size of the oil particles.
Determine the molecular weights of hydrogen and nitrogen.
What is the amount of substance (in moles) in $1$ g of water?
How many molecules are there in $10$ g of oxygen?
The molar mass of nitrogen is $0.028$ kg/mol. What is the mass of a nitrogen molecule?
Why can two lead blocks with smooth, clean cut surfaces stick together when pressed against each other?
Determine the number of atoms in $1$ m$^3$ of copper. The molar mass of copper is $\mu=0.0635$ kg/mol, and its density is $\rho=9000$ kg/m$^3$.
Diamond has a density of $3500$ kg/m$^3$. What volume do $10^{22}$ diamond atoms occupy?
